title: gave a coding agent godotiq and it built a whole 3d platformer on its own, no human placed a single node
author: jf_nash
selftext:
i wanted to see how far a coding agent could get building a real game on its own, so i gave claude godotiq and let it run. godotiq is the tool i make that gives the agent actual sight inside godot, it can see the 3d scene in space, place nodes, wire signals, check things at runtime. without it the agent is basically blind in there. that's the whole point of it.

what came out is marble gauntlet, a 3d marble platformer with two full levels, saws, spikes, a cannon that fires you across a gap, gems, best times. physics, camera, menus, sound, particles, hundreds of objects per level. the coding agent built every piece itself. no human placed a single node or wrote a line of gameplay code.

you can play it right on the homepage → [godotiq.com](http://godotiq.com)

to be clear it's just a demo, not a finished game. there's rough edges and stuff i'd do differently, left in on purpose to show what it does unsupervised. if i worked alongside it properly it'd come out way cleaner. and since it's my tool: the free tier covers a lot, a full game like this needs pro. just being straight.

comments.author: tymuska
comments.body: So for this, did you fine tune a model on godot and give it some state reading into the engine?

replies.author: jf_nash
replies.body: it's an mcp server. mcp is just an open protocol that lets an agent call external tools, works in cursor, windsurf, claude code, whatever, with any model. so godotiq isn't a model, it's a set of godot tools the agent can call: scene\_map, placement, run, screenshot and so on. agent asks, my server reads the project and the running engine, hands back the spatial data and live state. that's how gpt gets in too, you just run it in an mcp client and the tools show up.

comments.author: Ill-Past4609
comments.body: Yeah been using Godot and sometimes the Ai doesn’t get it right. Just need to be more specific sometimes, I get mad and just do it manually if I see after the 2nd time it’s not working

replies.author: jf_nash
replies.body: yeah that's the exact loop, and the "give up after two tries and do it by hand" part is the real cost, you stop being the director and turn into the cleanup crew. thing is being more specific only goes so far, the agent still can't see the scene so it's guessing no matter how clear you are. that's the bit godotiq fixes, it feeds the actual scene back so it stops guessing and you stop having to take over. what kind of stuff did you end up doing by hand most?

comments.author: slipperyslips
comments.body: Yooo just bought ur tool a moment ago. Mostly cause you mentioned it can see the live godot world. Any other sleeper features in here?

replies.author: jf_nash
replies.body:
yooo nice, thanks man, hope it earns its keep.

couple sleepers yeah. the live world stuff goes further than you think, it can actually prove a platform or enemy really moves instead of just writing code that looks right, and it can fake clicks so it tests your ui like a player would. then impact_check tells it what’ll break before it touches a signal, and trace_flow chases a bug across files when something shows wrong, way better than grepping for an hour.

and you don’t gotta remember any of the tool names, it just reaches for them on its own. so just build normally and it grabs what it needs. lmk what you make, and ping me if anything breaks

replies.author: slipperyslips
replies.body: Idk, i could probably leave a comment that adds nothing to the convo. But it looks likes you do that plenty for me. If youre curious to how i like the tool so far. Even though ive had it for literaly a day. It seems to be a good addition into my current QA workflow. Now codex can investigste remaining collision issues i have on terrain without it handing me the scene and asking for review, which would then be me spot checking areas, recording xyz cords that show visable issues and note likely causes. Now it will investigate changes visually. So its not "here human check this for seems or clipping" and instead "hey theres a terrain seem here, investigating, fixed." Before the handoff.
